# report

```go
import "github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/report"
```

Package report renders \[\]spec.Violation for humans and for machines.

It exists so that every yedit\-based tool can offer the same "validate my config" command without rewriting the grouping and formatting each time, and so that the JSON produced by those commands has one shape that a single CI parser can consume across all of them.

The validate package stays free of any rendering dependency: importing report is opt\-in, and a headless validation run that only inspects the returned violations never links it.

### Severity

Reporters split violations by spec.Severity. Errors and warnings are counted and rendered separately, and JSON reports "valid" from the error count alone, so a warning never fails a build.

<a name="GroupBySection"></a>
## func [GroupBySection](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/report.go#L82>)

```go
func GroupBySection(violations []spec.Violation) (sections []string, bySection map[string][]spec.Violation)
```

GroupBySection buckets violations by Section. sections is sorted, so the output order is stable across runs.

<a name="JSON"></a>
## func [JSON](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/json.go#L33>)

```go
func JSON(w io.Writer, violations []spec.Violation, opts Options) error
```

JSON writes the report as indented JSON. Summary counts errors per top\-level section and is always present, so a consumer reading only the summary does not have to handle a missing key.

<a name="Plain"></a>
## func [Plain](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/plain.go#L15>)

```go
func Plain(w io.Writer, violations []spec.Violation, opts Options)
```

Plain writes an uncolored, one\-line\-per\-violation report: the path padded to a fixed column, then the message, then the counts. It is the format to pipe into grep, and the one to use when the output is not a terminal.

A run with no violations at all prints "ok".

<a name="Pretty"></a>
## func [Pretty](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/pretty.go#L46>)

```go
func Pretty(w io.Writer, violations []spec.Violation, opts Options)
```

Pretty writes a themed report: errors grouped by top\-level section as a tree, warnings listed after them, then a summary line per severity.

<a name="Section"></a>
## func [Section](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/report.go#L63>)

```go
func Section(path string) string
```

Section returns the top\-level section a violation path belongs to, or "\(general\)" for a document\-wide violation with no leading key.

<a name="SubPath"></a>
## func [SubPath](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/report.go#L73>)

```go
func SubPath(path string) string
```

SubPath strips the top\-level section from a violation path, leaving the part that is worth showing under a section heading. A path with no separator is returned unchanged.

<a name="Table"></a>
## func [Table](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/table.go#L31>)

```go
func Table(w io.Writer, violations []spec.Violation, opts Options)
```

Table writes errors as one bordered table per top\-level section, then the same summary lines Pretty produces. Warnings are listed as a tree rather than a table: they are rarely numerous enough to need columns.

This is the only reporter that costs a dependency \(go\-pretty\). Pretty covers the same ground without one.

<a name="JSONOutput"></a>
## type [JSONOutput](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/json.go#L15-L22>)

JSONOutput is the machine\-readable shape written by JSON.

It is the contract a CI job parses, so it is documented and stable: fields may be added, but the meaning of an existing one will not change. Valid is derived from the error count alone, so a warning never fails a build.

```go
type JSONOutput struct {
    Valid        bool            `json:"valid"`
    ErrorCount   int             `json:"error_count"`
    WarningCount int             `json:"warning_count"`
    Errors       []JSONViolation `json:"errors,omitempty"`
    Warnings     []JSONViolation `json:"warnings,omitempty"`
    Summary      map[string]int  `json:"summary"`
}
```

<a name="JSONViolation"></a>
## type [JSONViolation](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/json.go#L25-L28>)

JSONViolation is one violation in a JSONOutput.

type JSONViolation struct {

}

<a name="Options"></a>
## type [Options](<https://github.com/lucasassuncao/yedit/blob/main/report/report.go#L30-L45>)

Options tunes the reporters. The zero value is valid: full detail, default theme, auto\-detected width.

```go
type Options struct {
    // SummaryOnly prints only the counts, omitting individual violations.
    SummaryOnly bool
    // Theme styles the structural parts of the output (section headings,
    // connectors, paths). Severity colors are deliberately not themed: an
    // error is red and a warning is yellow in every theme, the same rule the
    // alert component follows.
    Theme theme.Theme
    // WarningNote is appended to the warning summary line when non-empty, for
    // applications that want to say what their warnings mean
    // (e.g. "valid configuration that can lose files").
    WarningNote string
    // Width is the terminal width used by Table. Zero detects it from stdout
    // and falls back to 120.
    Width int
}
```
